clue.text: Get payback for turning up to promote German city

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards
promoting a letter means taking it out of its place and moving it up to the front of the word

parts.note: to avenge a wrong is to get payback for it
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Someone seeking revenge pushes the cause of a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: AVENGE read upwards is EGNEVA; its G (German) is then promoted to the top, giving GENEVA. 'German city' looks like one definition, but GENEVA is Swiss: the definition is just 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a major Swiss city on Lake Geneva, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: American frontier stew?

parts.note: surface reading: a hearty dish cooked by pioneers out on the American frontier
setter's reading: the answer, read as an instruction, makes the letters of its second word go wild, and they come out as the word stew

explanation.surface: A cowboy's pot of food simmering on the plains of the old frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay and 'stew' is its result. Making the second word 'wild' rearranges its letters into STEW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wild West is the name for the nineteenth-century western frontier region of the United States.

clue.text: Friends is returning with immediate impact? Absolutely

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word for friends is read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
a bang is a sudden, immediate impact

explanation.surface: A comment on the TV sitcom Friends making a big splash on its return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friends' with a capital looks like the sitcom, but it is just pals. The question mark flags that 'Absolutely' is used in its informal sense of 'exactly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-bang is an informal adverb meaning exactly or directly, as in slap-bang in the middle, much like absolutely.

clue.text: Millions in bed over the festive period?

indicators.note: one thing in another means it is placed inside, so the abbreviation goes within the word for a bed

parts.note: a crib is a child's bed
M is the abbreviation for million(s)
O is the cricket-scoring abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Millions of people lie in bed all through Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIMBO is British slang for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimbo is a colloquial British word for Christmas, the festive season of the year.

clue.text: "Mine," repeatedly claims songwriter

indicators.note: to claim something is to lay hold of part of it, so only a run of letters from inside the repeated word is kept

parts.note: the quoted word written out three times in a row

explanation.surface: A songwriter keeps insisting that the work is his own, saying 'Mine, mine'.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the joins of the repeated word: min(E MINEM)ine, with the outer letters dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminem is the stage name of the American rapper Marshall Mathers, who writes his own songs.

clue.text: Organ put next to altar, initially

parts.note: to put something somewhere is to place it

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Instructions for positioning a church organ beside the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument in a church, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The placenta is a temporary organ in pregnancy that nourishes the foetus through the umbilical cord.

clue.text: Bill's vice is returning in Spanish city

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the phrase built from the previous words is read backwards

parts.note: Al Gore was vice-president under Bill Clinton
to be is to exist, or live

explanation.surface: A man's vice resurfacing in a Spanish city, as if a lapsed sinner relapsed on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice' looks like a sin, but it means deputy: Bill Clinton's vice-president was Al Gore. AL LIVES read backwards gives SEVILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevilla is the Spanish spelling of Seville, the capital of Andalusia in southern Spain.

clue.text: Rabble-rousing nurses head off Mary Berry in Glasgow

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the stirred letters wrap around the single letter
rousing stirs things up, so the letters of the unruly crowd are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken off the following name

parts.note: the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A mob nursing TV baker Mary Berry, apparently somewhere in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mary Berry' reads as the TV baker, but it is split: Mary gives M, and 'Berry in Glasgow' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a bramble is the usual word for a blackberry, the fruit of the bramble bush.

clue.text: Double bluff?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The solver expects hidden wordplay in so short a clue, but there is none: the clue simply states its answer, which is itself the bluff, and the question mark admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A double bluff is a deception in which one tells the truth expecting the other to assume it is a lie.

clue.text: Prepare the way for metal pot somehow to hold uranium

indicators.note: holding something means taking it in, so the chemical symbol joins the cooking vessel's letters

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged freely

parts.note: taken as written
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Directions for a metal pot to be made to contain uranium.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that lead up to something come before it and pave the way for it to happen.

clue.text: Eat around one in site of Oktoberfest

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for eat goes on both sides of the numeral

parts.note: to munch is to eat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Eating your way around the beer festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Oktoberfest is the annual beer festival held in Munich, the capital of Bavaria.

clue.text: Reserve national team for national leader

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the second-string side behind the full Welsh rugby team
second meaning: Lech ..., the former president of Poland

explanation.surface: A substitute player stepping into the place of a country's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'A' team in rugby is a nation's reserve or development side, so the reserve Welsh side is WALES A.
explanation.definitionFit: Lech Walesa led the Solidarity trade union and was president of Poland from 1990 to 1995.

clue.text: Flipping bighead John Campbell?

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of big
john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
Ming is the nickname of Sir Menzies Campbell, the former Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: Calling a man named John Campbell a flipping bighead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bighead' looks like one insult, but only its head, B, is used. A loo is a British toilet; Menzies Campbell, pronounced Ming-is, is widely known as Ming.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British euphemisms used for emphasis in place of a swear word, as in a blooming nuisance.

clue.text: Caribbean Island accepts mistake, sick of opposition to the activity of partisans

definitions.text: opposition to the activity of partisans

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the island's name receives the other words inside it

parts.note: Antigua is an island in the Caribbean
to err is to make a mistake
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A Caribbean island owning up to an error, tired of being opposed by guerrilla fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick of' reads as fed up with, but 'sick' gives ILL and 'of' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiguerrilla describes action directed against guerrillas, irregular fighters also called partisans.

clue.text: Hoping to be American secret agents, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the words and listen to what they sound like

parts.note: A for American, plus a spy ring, a network of secret agents

explanation.surface: Someone who dreams of joining the CIA as a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the abbreviation for American.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiring actor is one hoping to become an actor, so the adjective means ambitious to be something.

clue.text: I traded with a crook, and beamed

indicators.note: a crook is bent, and bent letters are twisted out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trader admits dealing with a criminal and grins about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beamed' looks like smiled, but it is the sense of sending out rays.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to send out light or energy in rays, which is to beam.

clue.text: Delivery left for one dodgy baker

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: e.g. means for example, for one
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy baker's bread delivery left on the doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg break is a cricket delivery spun by the bowler so it turns from the leg side toward the off side.

clue.text: Free oil on tap is not compulsory

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can fall any way

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Free oil from a tap that nobody is forced to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional may be chosen or not, so it is not required.

clue.text: Pay no attention to topless foreign eccentric (or topless foreign man)

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put into an odd order
topless means the top, in a down clue the first letter, is removed

parts.note: taken as written, before beheading

explanation.surface: Snub the odd foreigner, whether shirtless or not.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket gives a second route: a foreign man could be an Italian signore, and without its S that is IGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it and take no notice of it.

clue.text: Delicate point raised in church extremely tetchily

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the short word is written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sensitive matter brought up very irritably in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine or subtle distinction, a delicate detail.

clue.text: Partygate in magistrate's office

parts.note: a do is a party; the first half of the compound word
the second half of the compound word, taken as written

explanation.surface: The Downing Street lockdown parties scandal, set in a magistrate's office.
explanation.walkthrough: Partygate was the 2021-22 scandal over parties held in Downing Street during Covid lockdowns; the setter splits the one word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogate is the office or rule of a doge, the chief magistrate of the old Venetian and Genoese republics.

clue.text: Leather worker in 6d

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who cures hides into leather
second meaning: sixpence, written 6d in old British money

explanation.walkthrough: '6d' looks like a cross-reference to 6-down, but it is six old pence; a tanner was the slang name for the British sixpence coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanner turns animal hides into leather, and tanner was old slang for a sixpenny coin.

clue.text: Dry Fe(III)?

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
in chemistry, the -ic suffix marks the higher oxidation state, so iron(III) is ferric

explanation.walkthrough: Iron(III) compounds are called ferric, so the Roman numeral stands for the suffix -IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry humour is wry and understated, which is what ironic means when describing a remark.

clue.text: Highlight organised demonstration's centrepiece being outrageous

parts.note: to flag something is to highlight it
to run an event is to organise it

indicators.note: a centrepiece is what stands in the middle, so the central letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of the thirteen

explanation.surface: Pointing out that the core of a planned protest is scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised demonstration' reads as one phrase, but 'organised' is RAN on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant offence is glaring and shocking, so outrageous in its openness.

clue.text: I'm not obliged, but try to leave the cost, generally

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters are removed from the longer phrase

parts.note: the going rate is the usual or general price
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Someone owes nothing, but tries to walk out without paying the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: GOING RATE with GO taken out leaves INGRATE. The definition is the attitude of the answer speaking: an ungrateful person feels no obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, one who feels no sense of being obliged to a benefactor.

clue.text: Supports welcoming a recipient of bequest

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the supports enclose the single letter

parts.note: a leg and a golf tee are both things that support
taken as written

explanation.surface: Supporters welcome a beneficiary of a will.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Supports' stands for two different supports, a leg and a golf tee, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who receives a legacy, money or property left in a will.
